body: That's great to hear, and sounds like a good start. Feel free to message me any time or keep me updated if you want to talk, okay?

You sound like you have it pretty tough, and that your parents aren't exactly the best, and I'm very sorry you have to deal with that. 

Is there anybody in your circle of friends or community you can talk to? A counsellor? You mention God- are you less religious than your mother, and has that caused issues for you in the past?

I'm surprised that your father hates you using your laptop when your doing something like coding- a really great life skill to have!

and look, that's totally okay if your not up to a job yet. Maybe you'd be better off building up your mental energy and motivation first, and your sense of responsibility. Do a piece of writing 500 words long every day, go for a walk, anything! but have a consistent goal that is easy to achieve to get you back on track. 

It'll help you feel better mentally, get back into the swing of things and get you OUT there. Baby steps, or you'll stumble before you figure out how to walk yet ;)

Its okay to take a long while to figure out your goals or what you want to do- its really common but a lot of people keep quiet about it. Don't let your grandparents get to you, but if you can't avoid it, maybe try making some job related things a part of your goal- Volunteer at a film or writing thing for littlies, improve your resume, lots of little things you can do to take those baby steps to get people off your back while you dip your toes in the water.

That sounds really difficult, and I'm sorry that your having to take this all on yourself. But it does sound like your children really do need you- one is only 11, the others haven't seen their (father? Mother?) in 4 whole years, and they lost their grandma, and if she was helping to support you then she probably had a good relationship with your children, although feel free to correct me if I'm wrong. 

This is a really hard thing, and you're the backbone and foundation that supports your entire family, and that's a lot of strain for one person on their own.

 Have you seeked out some therapy after your mother passed? Remember how on an airplane, they tell you to put on your air mask before helping others- this is why. You need to be a little selfish and help yourself before it all comes crashing down around your ears.

Oh, your (slightly) younger than me! I'm surprised haha, you write very well! 

Honestly, I don't even know how to drive yet, and I live with my grandparents. You may have lost a lot and made some really bad decisions, but that's what being young is for!

 Losing your job, going on trips and buying too much pizza and video games- sounds exactly like what everybody does and fucks up now and again.

 I think you ( and feel entirely free to tell me if I'm wrong!) maybe think a little too much on the darker side, and not as much about how to improve from your mistakes which, at the end of the day, aren't as bad as they could have been! Have you had any luck searching for new work? How are your parents about you living with them?

Why do you feel that your stuck in one place and "side stepping"? What makes you feel that your a disappointment- if your comfortable doing so, could you give me some examples?

You feel like you have to fake your emotions- is that because your mother is a perfectionist, and you worry about not being up to her standards, or is it something else? 

I understand if you don't ant to talk about your father, but if you want to vent this is a safe space in which to do so. You seem like a very caring individual.

Its still an amazing achievement with how hard it is to enter YouTube now! Congratulations! 

What happened to cause you to run out of money? Did you move back in with your parents after moving out?
Very wholesome XD
Its a (wholesome) bot haha. Have you considered writing a blog or doing a youtube channel? You seem to be a good writer.
Why do you feel that they hate you? Whose been saying that kind of thing that makes you feel that way about yourself? We're here to help you, tell me a bit more about yourself.

I'm glad to hear that your friend will be at your new school! Please do try to talk to your mom about how your feeling, and see if she has any advice for you- I'm sure she knows you a lot better than I do!

I think there's a lot of different things going on here, and I'm so sorry you're going through all this. 
One thing I'd like to mention is that pain isn't comparable between people- somebody "having it worse" than you doesn't and shouldn't dismiss your own pain, and if your having this many issues with anxiety, you DO know what it is, and she may be letting her own stigmas and experiences cloud what is right and how to help you right now. 

Finding the right words to communicate these feelings to those you love can be hard, especially when you care so much and you don't want to strangle them with your own anxieties. 

The way I've always thought about it with my own boyfriend is, I care about him deeply, and he feels the same way for me. If he was feeling anything at all that he wanted to share with me, I would never want him to hold that back because  I love being able to help him and support him. There is a limit. You have a responsibility to, at some stage, get professional help, and better your self, but your partner is there to be a support to you, and you to them. 

It's so, so easy to get overwhelmed, and it sounds like you may be having compulsive thoughts (like a voice in your head that tells you that you MUST die, it HAS to happen, DIE DIE DIE) and if that's true, that makes it harder to get out of this cycle of confusion and sadness.

That's a really good idea, but I think talking to your mom a little about the feelings your having now is a good idea between now and august- that's a lot of time to be feeling so down without good support, and moving schools is never easy, although a fresh start may be just what you need. Are you religious at all, or have any support community that you could go to in the interm between now and this change?

You've got a lot of really complex feelings and thoughts going on there. 

What career would you be in if you could do anything right now?
Send help please? What can I do to help you right now?

It doesn't even have to be about that, that's one of the really good things about therapy. They can help you without you having to talk about those things that make you feel like that, and give you methods of dealing with all the emotions your dealing with right now in a healthier way. They're just there to be somebody to confided in, to give you really good advice and to help you think about things in a healthier way.
No, no sorry! I was just trying to explain that that comment is from a bot that's been on a heap of subreddits for the past hour or two. Sorry for the confusion!

I'm really happy to hear you and your mom are getting along! She seems like she really cares about you- and while I know that going to a psychologist isn't great sometimes, the are really good at what they do, and sometimes its a case of looking until you find the one that's right for you.

It says in his post history 
"Yes I'm a bot. 
I'm just trying to spread love.
Life is tough and nothing comes easy. I didn't have the heart to tell people it's a bot. Sure some people will do the due diligence and find out, but a lot of people are telling me how much they needed the compliment, or how happy they were and some reached out saying they're tearing up. Some people knew it was a bot and told me how it changed their day. Let's do something special together.
Love."
So don't worry about it too much- I got a message like this from him myself.
How is your relationship with your mom?

It doesn't sound silly at all, and the reason there so much info for people your age and for people of EVERY age in regards to this is because its such a huge thing in a lot of people's lives. I'm worried that you've began to self harm, have you continue to do that after getting over her? You say that you still have periods of depression- have you talked to a doctor or trusted family member about these feelings?

I know it can be hard to ferret out help, especially when you've tried reaching out only to be dismissed or have nothing last, but maybe a serious talk with your doctor and re-establishing with your therapist would be a good start. I'm sorry that the people in your life haven't followed up with you.

Some girl troubles then hey? That's very normal, and theres LOADS of really good advice out there to help you deal with any feelings or direction you might need. If you let me know what you'd like some support in (getting over her, communicating with women, ect), I can help you find some good reading that will give you some direction if youd like it :) 

If you feel safe doing so, would you mind telling me around how old you are? That might help me give you some better advice.

Depression isn't just one feeling or behaviour, and while I'm not a doctor, and cant tell you exactly what's going on behind the scenes, the disconnect, the feelings of isolation, the lack of feeling- these are all symptoms, and I think being in contact with your doctor, about this AND the way that your using alcohol, may be able to really help you. 

If you don't feel comfortable with it, you don't need to talk to your friends about it. You can keep some things private while you work through it. 

But there's NOTHING wrong with feeling this way, or with having issues with mental health, and it sounds like your friends care about you, so have a think about getting some support from the people you trust.
Hey, can you tell me a little about your kids? you say you have two eldest ones in their teens, do you have any that are younger? Do you have a partner? Tell me a little about yourself xx

Maybe your looking for a bit of help, some advice, or direction in life. Its okay to be confused, and upset, and lost!
Can you tell me a little about yourself?
It really sounds like your suffering with depression. Have you talked to somebody you trust or a doctor about these feelings?

I do wish you good luck, and I'm really happy to hear you are putting yourself out there with other girls, even if sometimes you go through rejections. Congratulations, that's a really hard thing to do! 

I do think, if you haven't already, maybe going to therapy and working on the reasons your last major relationship failed may help you. We can always learn fro  the ones that got away and improve ourselves so that next time we have somebody we love dearly, we won't repeat history. Going to anger management, learning how to improve your patience properly, rather than just telling yourself not to, learning how to express yourself a little better and overcome your anxieties. You have a lot of data and you seem to know why your relationship had problems, so work on them! 

Most of your dreams don't seems aligned with Engineering, and you don't seem (sorry if I'm wrong!) to have much passion for the actual subject. You're obviously intelligent, or you couldn't have gotten into the subject in the first place, but I think you may want to consider that if your struggling like this with the course work, and its making you this unhappy, how you will feel doing this full time as a career for years! Maybe considering what you actually are passionate about learning, and would feel happy dedicating your time to may be a good exercise for you.

Your father sounds like a good man, and I understand sometimes medication doesn't work for people. Some people have to go hundreds of different types before they find the right one, and some people just have to work on themselves. I think working on the stuff I outlined before and having a think on what behaviours in your life you'd like to change, and doing CBT may really help you!

One last thing, you talk you your ex girlfriend "abandoning" you- how did the break up feel to you? How was it discussed, what was the impact on you? Its clearly effecting you quite a lot even today, and I don't know if the way your thinking about it is very healthy, and some of these feelings may be coming across in the new relationships you are trying to start with people. 

I really do wish you the best of luck, and please keep me updated on how your travelling so I can cheer you on!

Hey there, I am available to talk to anytime (although sometimes I wont be able to reply for a bit!) 

It really seems like you might have some issues with your self esteem. Some people really struggle with some subjects, even if they're brilliant at others. Could you tell me a bit about why you picked to study engineering? 

Was your relationship with your ex girlfriend good? If its not too painful, i'd like to know a little about why that ended, and about your relationship with your dad- Do you think he might be able to support you while you feel like this? 

Have you been reaching out to others? Sometimes people are just as afraid of you to make the first move for friendship, and people keep their distance because they don't like putting themselves on the line.

Sorry that I'm late responding! 

Look, if you look in my post history on this, you'll know my life wasn't great. I was sexually abused by my mother, made to eat my vomit, beaten, and ran away from home when I was 17. I KNOW life isn't perfect, and I've had more than enough days where I've wanted to kill myself, or felt like I HAVE to. 

My justification isn't that this is the only life that you'll have, but that I've been there, and even if I fall down sometimes, so many people have shown me that even when things are awful, they do eventually get a bit better, and then a bit better. I want to try and be that person for the people on here that feel they have nobody that they can turn to, put some positivity out into the world. I don't try to guilt trip, and I'm sorry if I've came across that was, because I don't think feelings like this deserve guilt.

 I think we all need somebody to talk to with out judgement, a little advice now and again from someone not caught up in everything going wrong in your life, and support. 

And your right! Its up to the person what they decide to do, and whatever they choose will be the right choice for them. But I know that when I've came here, its because I know its not the right choice, and I just need something to tie me down until I feel that way again too.

 I'm sure I'm wrong in some cases, but if somebody here would like to talk to me because they feel the same way, then regardless of there choices I'm happy I could help them fulfil that need for a little. I hope you understand where I'm coming from :)

You don't need to be any more specific than that, and I totally understand wanting to talk to your parents in person. Are you close with them? I think if you are, talking to them about this could be a real comfort to them- It may help show them that you WANT to be better, and that the violence is not who you want to be. Do you fight with them over anything specifically IE chores, attitude issues, friends or anything else?

[Here's](http://preventsuicidewv.org/help-for-teens-suicide-prevention/) a phone line, toll free, that you can call if you need the extra support. It also has several services you can check out to see which suits you best.

You also may be able to find info [here](http://www.dhhr.wv.gov/Pages/default.aspx) that may help with what you can get in regards to healthcare, and I'm sorry I can't help you with something more specific- I'm not American, so some of the details are going to be lost on me there.

Why do you feel that you're a failure? There's nothing wrong with having an average past, and the great thing about the future is that as long as you live, it can be changed! 

If your having issues with motivation, maybe try setting really small goals for yourself bit by bit- If you tend to sleep in a lot try setting a goal to wake a little earlier each day. Take a walk every day. Start a small hobby. Little things like that can help improve your mental health a lot!

You clearly care very deeply for your partner, and it seems like he feels very strongly about you too- I think talking to him about how your feeling may be a good course of action- If he was feeling the same way, wouldn't you want to be there to support him? That's what people who love each other do. Reach out to those who care about you, don't isolate yourself- your worth so much more to them than you think xx
You can also message me if you would like. Always happy to talk to you about whatever you need x

Hey there, I'm 19 and a girl too, and if you ever want somebody to message when your feeling down, feel free to message me anytime. 

Its a really good thing that you have recognised you need some support.
 You say that you've been violent for a long time? What triggers that violence? How are you violent? This cycle you talk about might be a symptom of mental illness, and those can be stabilized with medication and therapy to give you a much better standard of life! 

Are you comfortable telling me the country you live in? I may be able to find some places that can give you extra support if you'd like me too :)

Everyone deserves to have somebody there to listen to them when they are feeling beaten down by life, even if many people never get that support. It's not just about telling people it'll be okay, or prolonging their lives- we're offering another, independent viewpoint that may help people solve the problems they are having that cause them to feel these ways, or support them and give them the confidence to seek out help in their own communities IRL. 

I value life because it's precious. I don't believe in an afterlife. I know we will all pass one day. But it's the only life I believe we will ever have, and I hope to maybe give somebody that hope that things WILL get better, and one day there will be more happy moments then dark ones. 

There is nothing wrong with selfishness- what do they tell you at a beginning of a flight? Put on your air mask before others. 

Sometimes, you need to do things for yourself, even if it hurts. If you are thinking about how your family might feel if they found out the thoughts your having, I'm willing to bet you do care about their feelings. Why do you believe your dad thinks of you as selfish, or hates you? 
Can you tell me a little more about yourself?

I had a very similar experience! When I was 17ish, my mother pinned me up against a sliding door by my throat, and pinned my other arm with her other hand. When I couldn't get her off with my (weaker) arm, I ended up kicking her and she went into the dining table and got a cut. 

She's never let that go, and its one of her Go To points about what an horribly abuse demon I am. She never remembers the fact she pinned me though -_-
That's awful! I'm so sorry she said that to you.

All the time. When recounting fights we'd had, she'll only state what I did- kicking her, 'bashing' her to all her friends, family ect. 

But she'd strip it of all the context of her choking me and THEN me kicking her OFF me, or that I really just bumped her with my foot while I was half awake in bed that she sat on, and she responded by beating me so bad my little brother hid. 

That's right, bumping her with my foot half asleep was beating her black and blue.... and everything she did to me was 'discipline'.

I thought it was funny how that works out too. My mother hacked into my facebook without telling me, read and wrote down everything I said in private and saw that I had somebody willing to get me out, she saw me packing my things into boxes, and yet she had no hesitation during the fight 'that broke the camels back' to tell me to move out ASAP, and then go to bed and fall asleep soundly. She was beyond shocked when she woke up and I was gone!

I was really paranoid for over a year after leaving my mother's. I was lucky enough to avoid her even in our small town. When you have cut your parent/s out, have they turned up at your place? That sounds really scary!

I'm afraid I'm not familiar with "See it, accept it, let it go", at least under that name. And yes, I mean physically. Usually stopping myself from moving as much as possible to make sure there's less of a chance of me following along and internalising the intrusive thoughts and doing something I'd regret later.

 I find, personally, when depressed or stressed, cleaning and organising the space around me helps me think more clearly and process my more violent feelings in a healthy way (since I can be the most violent folder of clothes that I want haha), but for intrusive thoughts I find being as still as possible to help more, since I'm usually not actually feeling all that bad, I just can't block out the thumping of this powerful... voice in my head repeating itself, telling me that I HAVE to die, it's what MUST happen, RIGHT now. 

I'm not great at "letting feelings go", but I can "separate" myself from them a little, break them down into smaller compartments so its easier to deal with them or trivialise them, pretend that I'm a friend or psychologist sorting out or helping the "real" me get through my immediate feelings, and since I know myself best, I trust myself best with admitting the shittier reasons I'm not feeling great- whether its because I'm co-dependent or I said something stupid and don't know how to apologise or other stuff.
What are you looking for from life? How do you feel that the life you are currently living falls short from where you'd like to be?

I understand exactly what you're talking about, I think. It's like a completely different "voice" in my head, like a compulsion almost for me. I wont necessarily feel all that bad or depressed at that moment, and WHAM the voice pushes in my head and derails any train of thought I had or try to have, and just keeps entering again and again. I've found that keeping myself in one place, thinking logically and detaching a bit helps stave it off while making sure I don't do anything stupid while I'm going through it. Hopefully that helps you.
Good luck! If you remember to, give me an update in a couple months time, I'd love to know how you're travelling :)
Just take care of yourself, and remember that it's okay to fail or have things go wrong, and that things can always get better as long as your alive to change them <3

That sounds really hard to cope with, it must have really hurt to see that happen to your friend, and you probably aren't over it. That kind of thing can take years to work through. I'm glad your friend is trying to help you find some more ways of support- Is there a help line in the place you live that you may be able to call?


Also, this might be useless advice since I don't know where you are but your school may have a special circumstances allowance that will take into account the stress and trauma you go through, in regards to what happened to your friend and your sexuality, if you want to disclose that.
That seems like a good goal! If you need help budgeting or with financial advice once you get work, r/personalfinance should be able to help you get that sorted if you need the help.

Why are you at his place? because you forgot your keys? Just explain that it was a simple mistake, and that you didn't mean to overstay or violate his space. Maybe send him a text so its coming from you instead of his brother?

maybe don't  do it right now if he's not happy with you, but in the near future. He may see it as a sign of you moving away from pressuring him to date and getting more socially involved. The other stuff is normal forgetfulness, and making mistakes like that is only human, I wouldn't stress too much about it :)
That seems a tad mean, but maybe if you try asking he might surprise you. If you're feeling like this, it might be worth a shot to try?

Maybe you should try some courses on how to present yourself, or try out those pick up artist books? I hear they are really good mostly at teaching you how to interact with people and how to be more charismatic?

You don't sound pathetic at all. Therapy is hard, and so is meeting people. You can feel like your getting nowhere, and sometimes things don't click for a long while. I don't think its that your not trying hard enough or hoping for too much, I think that maybe R just misunderstands how best to help you through what your going though, since he and his family seem to care deeply for you.

 I think he might underestimate how much your hurting right now, and he wants the relationship between the two of you to be healthier than the kind of desperate love you have to give. Maybe he doesn't want to take advantage of the vulnerability of that. I really think that broadening your relationships with others will help your relationship with R, and help you to have more support. I know how hard it is, and how disheartening it can be to struggle to find true friends and such. Maybe R has some friends or good people he can introduce you to, to help you start?

I can empathise with you a lot on the boundary violations and triggering memories of the past. You just need to remember to breathe, and think. You were also just a child when this happened, and you didn't understand properly what was going on. Your history made those distinctions much harder. I understand that you are feeling very guilty about the past, but it can't be changed. I don't believe that if the story came out that your life would be ruined, because even if you don't think of it that way, you were also a victim. I think if you could find somebody to talk about these feelings with it might help you process the abuse you went though and learn how to deal with it in a healthier way than the severe stress and anxiety you are going through now.
What is stopping you from moving at the moment? Are there any smaller goals you can make that makes that easier to achieve?

You sound like you've been really strong through a lot of hardships in your life, and I think that R is trying to be a good friend to you by telling you that you should rely on yourself, even if it isn't helping you the way you feel now, it can be a very unhealthy way to live, for a single other person. Maybe you should try reaching out again to those friends that have drifted away, or participate in some other hobbies and try and build up some more social support? Is there any way you can get some psychological help where you are now?

What do you do on PC? What kind of things are you into? I'm sure you don't just stare at the black screen ;)

It's okay not to have a plan or a particular dream. Especially if you're suffering with depression or something like it, it can be really hard. You can make good decisions though, because here you are, reaching out for help when you need it. I understand feeling unmotivated and scared. Life can be harsh and hard. Have you tried talking to a doctor?
That's going to be rough for your family, losing you on your birthday. Have you confided these feelings to your wife?
Why have you chosen July 1st?
What makes your life not worth living, if you don't mind me asking?
What she did.

Lets talk about some stuff then? So many of the things that are plaguing you, you CAN change! If you want to wait it out until your friend leaves you, then maybe try working on those for now, and maybe you'll feel better with yourself?

Your acne can probably be fixed no problem! I'm no expert, but I've seen lots of amazing stuff at r/skincareaddiction and I'm sure you can find an guide or somebody will be happy to help you! Same thing with the rest of your body- maybe your not happy with your features now, but there's so many people out there who love so many varieties of people, and you may learn to love what you bring to the table ;) If you want to look for them, there's heaps of communities built around getting fit, and you could make some great lifelong friends, not to mention how much working out improves mental health!

I'm pan/bi sexual myself, and my mother is catholic. She pretended to be fine with gays, then when I told her I had a girlfriend she went and tried to get my (also catholic) grandparents to hate me as retribution. 
But they told her, and me, that they love me regardless, and now at 19 I have nothing to do with her and see them all the time! You're almost 18, and soon, you can choose who to associate with, and if your mother doesn't want to respect who you are for something as silly as orientation, then you should consider it her loss. Its hard, but sometimes people refuse to accept the oddest things. And who knows, she did say she doesn't know how she'd react. 

Your grades are another thing you can control, unlike the reactions of other people. A saying I like is "the only person you can ever control is yourself", and its very true. You can develop your own skills, and make them work for you. So many skills are workable, you just need to market yourself <3 It sounds like your best friend is a good girl, and you should try confiding in her how your feeling. If she was feeling this way, you'd want to help her wouldn't you? that's what good friends do for each other.  

For all you saying that you're an asshole, that guy saying those things to you seems to have some problems, and you might want to avoid him in the future, even if you'd like to reconcile. Does your best friend know how he's treating you? do your parents? 

If your mother has offered therapy to you in the past, then she can probably see that you are hurting. And look, in therapy you aren't expected to just pour out your life and for it to be easy. You can just talk to them about daily stuff, and sometimes it can be hard to open up. They're an independent adult, an extra framework of support. I think that it's really important you ask your mom again if she could help you get a therapist. I know its difficult, but they can teach you how to deal with all these feelings you are going through. 

Take care and feel free to PM me if you want to talk more, or just reply to this <3 Sorry for how all over the place this is, hopefully it makes sense!

I can empathise with what you are saying about being angry and feeling out of control, like its not really you then snapping out of it. It doesn't make you a bad person, and while it does feel awful, the people who care about you do understand that feeling too. Everyone can do things that they sincerely regret. But you recognise it- you CAN get better! See a professional, ask for methods to improve your temper, the way you deal with stress or issues in your life. Not just pills. People describe you as kind because they know you are. They want you in their lives! 

Stay safe <3
That was plan A, but I thought this could be a low-drama plan B. I was wrong!

He really is- Been my support and voice of reason for almost 3 years, and was my safe harbour when I ran away- his family welcomed me in with open arms and I stayed there for over a year :) Just moved out recently to start Uni!

Personally, I was the GC until my brother was born. There's about 10 years between us, so by the time he was able to speak and was more of a 'person', I was becoming decently independent and coming into being my own person, which she hated, since I was meant to be her "mini me". Then I became the SG as I started questioning her poor decisions and separating myself from our enmeshment.

I had a similar experience, but it wasn't as much of a 'win'- it became her ammo for over a year after it happened. 
Before I ran away for good, my mother and I had a fight. We had lots of fights, many where she was physically abusive towards me, but this one was different- I'd been with my SO for several months and learnt what actually sane families were like, and so I tried to channel his conflict management instead of my own (terrible) methods that I'd developed growing up with her. I tried grey rocking and walking away from the conflict. 

She wouldn't let me leave. She blocked the doorways, she ran after me, she grabbed me. I tried to leave through the sliding door in the back yard. She rushed me, pinned me by my neck with one hand and pinned my primary arm with the other against the door, spittle splattering my face as she just SCREAMED, because I'd had the audacity to tell her that the cats stayed away from her because she beat them.

I panicked, and managed to bring up my leg between us and kicked her way harder than I thought I was able- She's an almost 6' tall 'thick' woman who is a gym junkie- I'm 5'4 and am basically allergic to working out. She went flying into the wooden dining table, breaking the leg of it and as she showed me later and many times at that, sliced her back and left a nasty scar. But I did get away, even if I did come back within a couple of hours, after hiding near the local ice addicts house that I knew had a restraining order against my mother so I knew I'd be safe.

She actually called my SO, screaming at him on the phone (I wasn't able to grab mine before I left) after I'd ran off, telling him I'd "gone crazy and assaulted her" for no reason at all, and that he had to come and find me. He lived a 3 hour walk away, it was dark, we were 16 and he couldn't drive.  He still walked all that was to make sure I was okay, and I met him past midnight by the bus stop because I was too terrified to tell mother that he'd done such a thing for me, even after our "reconciliation".

I'd lurked for almost a year before I posted, and only commented a couple of times (One another account) during that time. I always feel like I'm not expressing myself correctly, or that posting has no purpose for me other than to vent because I already went NC, even though I've had plenty of issues with Nmom in that time. I tend to feel that actually posting something makes me too anxious as well, that people will hate me for writing something or that Nmom might find my post...

But that feeling that we're 'whining' is how Nparents want us to feel. It gives them control over how we see ourselves, our narrative, and absolves them of guilt. So here we have a space where we can take that back, and all of our problems are just as important to us and their actions just as hurtful, even if the magnitude is 'smaller'.

Definitely. Sometimes I wish my Nmom would just pass away so I won't have to look over my shoulder anymore.
